searchText: <@427491045308235776> seems that GLS254 doesn't have an implementation in Golang? At least I didn't see bindings from the assembly/C/Rust implementations. Incidentally, what is the implementation of Ristretto that I should be using? I see there's https://github.com/gtank/ristretto255 and there's https://github.com/bwesterb/go-ristretto where you yourself added code. This latter library does not have an explicit MSM implementation it seems and you need to loop, while the previous library relies on https://github.com/FiloSottile/edwards25519 which does have a variable time MSM it seems. It's driving me crazy that it seems that every single cryptographer that wanted to work with this curve reinvented the wheel instead of reuing code... which one should I be using? A quick look and it seems that ristretto255 is the right option - Yep the GLS254 doesn't have a golang impl - They both look interopable, I would use the gtank one if it has MSM -- I imagine that if we use Ristretto255, we would probably just re-implement the Ristretto part on top of stdlib and optimize the MSM algorithm there's no Ristretto on the std lib afaik Can you clarify, right now are the ristretto elements mostly zero bits? No they are random Ristretto is built ontop of edwards25519, which should be in the stdlib -- though yep the Ristretto part is not in the stdlib you can start with very small Ristretto scalars, but 1) they get multiplied in each hop and 2) you need to invert them Ah I see exactly, but the Ristretto255 library does not use the stdlib it uses the upstream fork which is more complete and is is against a previous version also not having a Golang impl is a killer for me, I' ll stick to Ristretto for the time being Yeah that should be updated I think I spoke too soon 🙂 The version in the golang stdlib is private, so they don't expose the necessary API, see `crypto/internal/fips140/edwards25519` So for updates, you would need to submit it to the golang stdlib, and then wait for the upstream fork to point to a newer version of the golang stdlib with that update

excerpts.author: kevaundray
excerpts.content:
- Yep the GLS254 doesn't have a golang impl

- They both look interopable, I would use the gtank one if it has MSM -- I imagine that if we use Ristretto255, we would probably just re-implement the Ristretto part on top of stdlib and optimize the MSM algorithm

excerpts.author: kevaundray
excerpts.content:
I spoke too soon 🙂 

The version in the golang stdlib is private, so they don't expose the necessary API, see `crypto/internal/fips140/edwards25519` 

So for updates, you would need to submit it to the golang stdlib, and then wait for the upstream fork to point to a newer version of the golang stdlib with that update
